# Adjudication Task — Chapter 614

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃614화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|띠링.
  6|
  7|
  8|
  9|- [동기화]를 시작합니다. 10, 9, 8, 7…… 1, 0.
 10|
 11|- [동기화]가 성공적으로 완료되었습니다. 갱신된 능력치가 신체에 적용되며, 특정 칭호에 한하여 사용이 제한됩니다.
 12|
 13|- [로그인]을 완료했습니다.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|익숙한 시스템 알림이 끝나기도 전에, 까슬까슬한 촉감과 젖은 풀잎 냄새가 피부와 코를 타고 전해져 온다.
 18|
 19|나는 입술에 붙어 있는 볏짚을 뱉어 내며 내심 중얼거렸다.
 20|
 21|‘돌아왔구나.’
 22|
 23|무림으로의 귀환.
 24|
 25|현대에서는 고작 한 달 남짓한 시간을 보냈을 뿐인데, 먼 과거의 일처럼 느껴지는 것은 결코 착각이 아니다.
 26|
 27|‘일이 하도 많았어야지.’
 28|
 29|무림. 그리고 현대.
 30|
 31|나와 두 세상을 둘러싼 모든 상황이 급변하고 있었다. 연이어 벌어지는 사건 속에서 몸이 두 개라도 부족할 지경이다.
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|다시 생각해 보니까 두 개는 맞구나. 그걸 번갈아 가며 컨트롤해야 하는 거라 더럽게 피곤한 거지.
 36|
 37|그나저나…….
 38|
 39|‘아. 일어나기 싫다.’
 40|
 41|전신을 감싼 볏짚은 생각 이상으로 따뜻하면서 푹신했다.
 42|
 43|이대로 늘어지게 한숨 자고 싶은 마음이 간절하다. 보급형 무공을 만드느라 근 일주일 동안 잠도 제대로 자지 못했기 때문이다.
 44|
 45|다음 순간 두런두런 들려온 대화 소리만 아니었다면, 정말 그대로 잠들었을지도 몰랐다.
 46|
 47|“음. 조장님이 어떤 사람이냐고요?”
 48|
 49|“네, 예전부터 궁금했거든요. 아직 다른 두 사람도 안 와서 심심한 것도 있고. 송 호위도 그렇죠?”
 50|
 51|익숙한 목소리다. 혁무진과 주화란의 대화에 이어, 추혼객(抽魂客) 송일섬이 퉁명스럽게 대답했다.
 52|
 53|“난 별로 안 궁금하오.”
 54|
 55|“들었죠? 송 호위도 궁금하대요.”
 56|
 57|“아니, 안 궁금하다니까.”
 58|
 59|“은자 두 냥 더 드릴게요.”
 60|
 61|“……살짝 궁금해지는군.”
 62|
 63|저 돈에 미친 새끼.
 64|
 65|큰손 회장님의 은자 도네이션 한 방에 무릎을 꿇은 송일섬까지 가세하자, 혁무진의 머뭇거리는 목소리가 들려왔다.
 66|
 67|“음, 이거 대답하기 어려운데. 조장님은 아직 주무시는 거 확실하죠?”
 68|
 69|“네. 네.”
 70|
 71|“확실히 잠들어 있다. 호흡이 안정되어 있어.”
 72|
 73|“하긴 그렇겠네요. 한 번 잠들면 귀신이 업어 가도 모를 정도니까.”
 74|
 75|안정된 것 같은 소리 하고 있네.
 76|
 77|그건 내가 호흡을 조절해서 그런 거다. 개인적으로도 은근히 어떤 대답이 들려올지 궁금했으니까.
 78|
 79|그리고 나의 충실한 오른쪽 새끼발가락은 기대를 배신하지 않았다.
 80|
 81|“저희 조장님은 아주 그 유명한 그, 아주 유명한 어 뭐랄까…….”
 82|
 83|“잘생기고 헌앙한 후기지수?”
 84|
 85|맑고 고운 영창 피아노 같은 주화란의 물음에, 혁무진이 세상 단호한 어조로 대답했다.
 86|
 87|“씹새끼였죠.”
 88|
 89|“……아.”
 90|
 91|“……어.”
 92|
 93|“요즘에서야 열화신룡이니 뭐니 하지. 일이 년 전만 해도 그만한 씹새끼 찾는 것도 힘들었습니다. 매일같이 기루 가서 술 처먹고, 공금 훔쳐서 도박장에 뿌리고. 오죽하면 그때 당시 조장님 별호가…….”
 94|
 95|“야.”
 96|
 97|“맞습니다. 야왕(夜王)이었어요. 그쪽 분야에서는 십왕(十王)이 떼로 덤벼도 상대가 안 된다니까요. 밤마다 옆구리에 전낭 떡 하니 차고 위풍당당한 걸음으로 기루로 향할 때면 저랑 동료 수문위사들이 그랬습니다. 저 씹새끼 오늘도 천마군림보 쓴다고. 그나저나 송 대협께서는 견문이 넓어서 들어 보셨구나. 역시.”
 98|
 99|혁무진의 너스레에 송일섬이 떨떠름한 목소리로 대꾸했다.
100|
101|“그게 무슨 소리냐. 난 아무 말도 안 했는데.”
102|
103|“예?”
104|
105|“아무 말도 안 했다고.”
106|
107|“에이. 무슨 소리세요. 조금 전에 야라고 하셨잖아요.”
108|
109|“아니라니까.”
110|
111|“틀림없이 사내 목소리였는데요. 농담도, 참. 그럼 도대체 누가…….”
112|
113|길게 늘어지던 말꼬리가 뚝 끊겼다.
114|
115|짧지만 무거운 침묵이 흐른 뒤, 누군가의 손길이 내 얼굴을 덮은 볏짚을 조심스럽게 걷어냈다.
116|
117|부스럭. 스윽.
118|
119|시야를 가리고 있던 볏짚이 치워지고, 희미하게 비추는 달빛 아래로 두 개의 시선이 부딪친다.
120|
121|나는 사람 좋아 보이는 푸근한 웃음과 함께, 오랜만에 마주한 혁무진을 향해 인사를 건넸다.
122|
123|“야.”
124|
125|“…….”
126|
127|말없이 깊게 가라앉은 시선으로 나를 내려다보던 혁무진이 손에 든 볏짚을 다시 내 얼굴에 덮었다.
128|
129|마치 아무 일도 없던 것처럼, 아주 조심스럽게.
130|
131|“치워.”
132|
133|“달이 밝아서 그런가. 웬 환청이…….”
134|
135|“안 치우면 네 인생이 어두워진다. 치워.”
136|
137|“옙.”
138|
139|볏짚에서 느꼈던 훈훈한 온기는 이미 사라진 지 오래다.
140|
141|나는 엑소시스트에 의해 봉인되었다가 수백 년 만에 깨어난 흡혈귀처럼, 마차 짐칸에서 부스스 몸을 일으켰다.
142|
143|휘우우우.
144|
145|스산한 바람이 옷자락에 들러붙은 볏짚을 날려 보낸다.
146|
147|나와 시선이 마주친 주화란이 황급히 고개를 돌리고, 언제 피웠는지 모를 모닥불 근처에서 불을 쬐고 있던 송일섬은 갑자기 말에게 건초를 먹여야겠다는 혼잣말과 함께 엉덩이를 뗐다.
148|
149|그리고 일렁이는 불길을 받아 커진 내 그림자가, 한 사람을 향해 드리워졌다.
150|
151|“마지막으로 남길 말은?”
152|
153|나직한 내 물음에 혁무진이 침착하게 대답했다.
154|
155|“조장님, 이러지 마시고 제 말을 좀 들어 보십시오.”
156|
157|“그래서 물었잖아.”
158|
159|“마지막이라면서요. 마치 유언 같잖아요.”
160|
161|“유언 맞을걸.”
162|
163|“……아.”
164|
165|“아주 신이 났더라. 수하의 그런 모습에 조장으로서 참을 수 없는 기쁨을 느낀다.”
166|
167|반쯤은 사실이다. 정말 참을 수가 없었다.
168|
169|무림에서 개고생, 현대에서 개고생하고 잠도 못 잔 상태로 돌아왔는데 직속 수하가 뒷담화를 까고 있던 건에 대하여.
170|
171|그리고 이 라노벨 제목 같은 상황에 뒤따라온 감정의 이름은 분노였다.
172|
173|“얼굴, 팔, 다리, 복부, 등. 이 중 하나만 골라.”
174|
175|“혹시 그거, 제 사인(死因)입니까?”
176|
177|“죽이진 않고, 죽도록 때릴 거야.”
178|
179|잠깐 고민하던 혁무진이 대답했다.
180|
181|“복부로 하겠습니다.”
182|
183|“이유는?”
184|
185|“등의 상처는…… 무림인의 수치니까.”
186|
187|나는 녀석의 기개에 탄성을 내뱉었다.
188|
189|“지랄 염병을 떠는군.”
190|
191|“잘못한 건 사실이니 벌은 달게 받겠습니다. 오십시오.”
192|
193|“그럼 네가 복부를 골랐으니, 난 나머지를 고르겠다.”
194|
195|“예?”
196|
197|“뭐가 ‘예?’야. 너만 고르면 불공평하잖아. 나도 골라야 공평한 거지.”
198|
199|“아니, 잠깐만요. 도대체 그게 왜 공평…….”
200|
201|빡!
202|
203|강렬한 타격음.
204|
205|천천히 타들어가는 모닥불 위, 코피를 뿌리며 솟구친 한 사람의 그림자가 짙게 드리워진다.
206|
207|‘오자마자 주먹을 쓰게 되다니.’
208|
209|이곳은 안휘(安徽)와 호북(湖北). 하남(河南)으로 이어지는 접경지인 대별산(大別山).
210|
211|그리고 BGM처럼 잔잔하게 깔리는 혁무진의 비명을 듣고 저 멀리에서 다가오는 두 그림자는, 근본 없는 사파 나부랭이이자 화룡각의 마지막 구성원들이다.
212|
213|“……저자는 왜 맞고 있는 거지?”
214|
215|“태산이! 왔다!”
216|
217|마침내 한자리에 모인 화룡각 남만원정대에게, 나는 짧지만 강렬한 훈시를 남기고 돌아섰다.
218|
219|“자자, 이 새끼만 마저 패고 출발합시다.”
220|
221|반발은 없었다.
222|
223|지금의 나는 S급 헌터 진태경이 아니라, 정파 무림 제일의 후기지수인 열화신룡이자 저들의 직속 상관인 화룡각주 진태경이니까.
224|
225|뻐억!
226|
227|“억! 어어억!”
228|
229|난 무림이 참 좋다. 물론 개 같은 암천은 빼고.
230|
231|
232|
233|* * *
234|
235|
236|
237|그곳은 빛 한점 들어오지 않는 칠흑(漆黑)의 공간이었다.
238|
239|어떤 소리도, 생기도 느껴지지 않는 어둠 속에서 죽은 듯이 엎드린 인영(人影)들이 잘게 몸을 떨었다.
240|
241|그리고 다음 순간.
242|
243|“천상천하(天上天下)!”
244|
245|“만마앙복(萬魔仰服)!”
246|
247|하나의 목소리로 터져 나온 벼락같은 외침과 함께, 어둠 속에서 검붉은 불꽃이 솟구쳤다.
248|
249|화아아악!
250|
251|거세게 타오른 불의 고리.
252|
253|틀림없는 불꽃임에도 불구하고, 뼈마디에 사무칠 만한 한기를 뿜어내는 불길 너머로 누군가의 그림자가 일렁였다.
254|
255|- 오랜만이구나.
256|
257|사내인지, 여인인지. 혹은 젊은이인지, 늙은이인지. 그도 아니라면 그 목소리가 낮은지 높은지조차 구분할 수 없었다.
258|
259|그것은 실로 기이한 음성이었고, 큰 울림을 낳으며 사방에서 울려 퍼져 바닥에 엎드리고 있던 인영들을 옥죄었다.
260|
261|- 나의 종들아.
262|
263|그 짧은 한마디에 담긴 미증유의 거력(巨力) 앞에 모두가 몸을 떨었다.
264|
265|절대자에 대한 두려움으로, 혹은 자신들이 모시는 존재를 마주했다는 감격과 환희로.
266|
267|그렇기에 그들은 한목소리로 부르짖었다.
268|
269|“이 어리석고 미천한 종들이, 위대하신 천주(天主)를 배알하옵니다!”
270|
271|천주. 하늘의 주인.
272|
273|그 존재를 설명할 수 있는 단어는 오직 그것밖에는 없었다.
274|
275|누구보다 존엄하고 위대한 절대자. 구름 위 하늘은 그의 궁전이며, 하늘 아래 땅에 살아가는 모든 하찮은 것들은 천주의 종이요, 백성이었다.
276|
277|아니, 반드시 그렇게 만들어야 했다.
278|
279|- 얼마나 흘렀는가.
280|
281|살아 있는 신의 물음을 이해하지 못하는 자는 아무도 없었다.
282|
283|이 자리에 엎드린 이들은 감히 이루 말할 수 없을 만큼 헌신적이며, 충성스러운 천주의 종복들이었으니까.
284|
285|바닥 깊숙이 엎드려 있던 한 청년도 마찬가지였다.
286|
287|“위대하신 천주께서 마지막으로 깨어나신 그날로부터, 꼭 일백하고도 삼십육 일이 흘렀사옵니다!”
288|
289|청년의 힘찬 대답에, 거세게 타오르던 불길이 일렁였다.
290|
291|- 그래. 떠오르는구나. 서천(西天). 그 아이가 떠난 날이었지.
292|
293|“망극하옵니다!”
294|
295|청년을 필두로 다시 한번 거대한 외침이 터져 나왔다.
296|
297|처음과는 달리 부끄러움과 자책이 실린 외침이었다.
298|
299|서천마군과 그가 이끌던 암천의 일군(一群)이 사천당가에서 전멸했을 때, 그들은 그 예상치 못한 결과에 당황했고 깊이 잠들어 있던 주인을 깨워야 했다.
300|
301|“위대하신 천주시여. 두 번 다시…… 그런 일은 없을 것이옵니다.”
302|
303|청년의 악문 잇새 사이로 흘러나온 목소리에 다시 한번 불길이 흔들렸다.
304|
305|- 아니다. 부족한 너희를 믿은 내 과오일 뿐.
306|
307|“……!”
308|
309|- 혈주(血主). 부족한 것은 너도 마찬가지 아니더냐.
310|

“……Ah.”

[P74]
“You were having a great time. As your captain, I can’t tell you how happy it makes me to see my subordinate enjoying himself.”

[P75]
That was half true. I really couldn’t take it.

[P76]
I’d busted my ass in the Murim, busted my ass in the modern world, and come back without getting any sleep—only to find my own subordinate talking shit about me behind my back.

[P77]
It sounded like the title of a light novel. What I felt about it was rage.

[P78]
“Face, arms, legs, abdomen, back. Pick one.”

[P79]
“Are those my possible causes of death?”

[P80]
“I won’t kill you. I’ll just beat you like I’m trying to.”

[P81]
Mujin thought for a moment.

[P82]
“The abdomen.”

[P83]
“Why?”

[P84]
“Wounds on the back are… a martial artist’s shame.”

[P85]
I couldn’t help marveling at his resolve.

[P86]
“What a load of bullshit.”

[P87]
“I did wrong, so I’ll take my punishment. Come at me.”

[P88]
“Since you picked your abdomen, I’ll pick the rest.”

[P89]
“What?”

[P90]
“What do you mean, ‘what’? It wouldn’t be fair if only you got to choose. I should get a turn too.”

[P91]
“No, wait. How is that fair—”

[P92]
Wham!

[P93]
The blow cracked through the night.

[P94]
Above the slowly burning campfire, the shadow of a man soaring upward with blood spraying from his nose loomed large.

[P95]
*Back five minutes and I’m already using my fists.*

[P96]
We were on Mount Daebyeol, where Anhui and Hubei bordered Henan.

[P97]
Two figures approached from the distance, with Mujin’s screams providing the background music. They were the final members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion: a pair of rootless unorthodox faction nobodies.

[P98]
“……Why are they beating him?”

[P99]
“Taishan! Is here!”

[P100]
At last, every member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s Nanman expedition party was together. I gave them a short but stirring address and turned back to Mujin.

[P101]
“All right, let’s finish beating this bastard and get going.”

[P102]
Nobody objected.

[P103]
Right now, I wasn’t Jin Taekyung the S-rank Hunter. I was the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, the orthodox Murim’s greatest young prodigy, and Jin Taekyung, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master—their direct superior.

[P104]
Crack!

[P105]
“Urgh! Aaaagh!”

[P106]
I really do love the Murim. Except for that damned Dark Heaven.

[P107]
* * *

[P108]
Not a single ray of light reached that pitch-black place.

[P109]
In the darkness, where neither sound nor any sign of life could be felt, figures lay facedown and trembled.

[P110]
Then—

[P111]
“Heaven above, earth below!”

[P112]
“All demons bow in submission!”

[P113]
The cries erupted as one, thunderous. Crimson-black flames surged up from the darkness.

[P114]
Fwoosh!

[P115]
A ring of fire blazed fiercely. Yet despite being unmistakable flames, they gave off a chill that seeped into the bones. Beyond them, someone’s shadow wavered.

[P116]
—It has been a long time.

[P117]
Man or woman, young or old—even the pitch of the voice was impossible to tell.

[P118]
The strange voice resounded from every direction, pressing down on the figures prostrate on the floor.

[P119]
—My servants.

[P120]
Everyone trembled at the overwhelming power in those two words. Some shook with fear of the absolute being before them; others with joy and rapture at seeing the one they served.

[P121]
Together, they cried out.

[P122]
“These foolish, lowly servants humbly pay their respects to the great Lord of Heaven!”

[P123]
Lord of Heaven. Master of the heavens.

[P124]
No other words could describe him.

[P125]
An absolute being of unmatched dignity and greatness. The heavens above the clouds were his palace; every lowly creature on the earth below was his servant and subject.

[P126]
No. They would make it so.

[P127]
—How much time has passed?

[P128]
Every one of them understood the living god’s question. The figures prostrate before him were servants of the Lord of Heaven, loyal and devoted beyond words.

[P129]
The young man bowing low against the floor was no different.

[P130]
“Exactly one hundred and thirty-six days since the great Lord of Heaven last awoke!”

[P131]
The fierce flames wavered at his answer.

[P132]
—Yes. I remember. Western Heaven. That was the day the child left.

[P133]
“We are deeply ashamed!”

[P134]
Led by the young man, they cried out again. This time, shame and self-reproach filled their voices.

[P135]
When the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Dark Heaven forces under his command had been annihilated at the Sichuan Tang Clan, the unexpected defeat had thrown them into confusion. They had been forced to wake their master from his deep sleep.

[P136]
“Great Lord of Heaven, never again… will such a thing happen.”

[P137]
The words came through the young man’s clenched teeth. The flames stirred once more.

[P138]
—No. The mistake was mine, for trusting you despite your shortcomings.

[P139]
“……!”

[P140]
—Blood Lord. You have your own shortcomings, do you not?

[P141]
At that reprimand, more painful than any other, the young man’s eyes trembled.

[P142]
Blood Lord knew better than anyone what the master he worshiped meant.

[P143]
*Henan.*

[P144]
The day the orthodox Murim had named the Shaolin Bloodshed was one of the most painful memories of his life. He had accomplished far less than planned, and suffered the humiliation of leaving an arm behind.

[P145]
If he hadn’t at least brought back Shaolin’s sacred treasure, the Green Jade Buddha Staff… He didn’t want to think about it.

[P146]
*The Sword Saint. And Jin Taekyung.*

[P147]
Thinking of those two bastards made him want to kill. Even tearing them apart alive wouldn’t satisfy him.

[P148]
But a loyal servant must not show such thoughts before his master. Blood Lord barely suppressed his murderous intent and spoke.

[P149]
“P-Please forgive me.”

[P150]
Whoooong.

[P151]
A chilly wind swept through the darkness in place of an answer. Blood Lord and the others huddled lower.

[P152]
Then a quiet voice reached their ears.

[P153]
—What is lacking can be filled.

[P154]
The air grew heavy. The wind stopped, and every living thing held its breath.

[P155]
In the stillness, the Lord of Heaven continued.

[P156]
—I shall fill what you lack.

[P157]
It was a command, backed by a force none of them could resist.

[P158]
Fwoooooosh.

[P159]
Darkness and shadow rippled.

[P160]
An immense surge of qi flowed from somewhere unseen and settled into Blood Lord’s body. His eyes widened with rapture.

[P161]
“L-Lord of Heaven!”

[P162]
Blood Lord and the others understood once more: the master they served was a living god, an absolute being who encompassed heaven and earth.

[P163]
They understood, too, what the power he had bestowed on them meant.

[P164]
—Tell South Heaven and North Heaven.

[P165]
Rumble, rumble, rumble!

[P166]
The earth trembled. The world shook.

[P167]
Beyond the overwhelming energy that distorted everything, his voice rang out like thunder.

[P168]
—Now… we begin the Great War.

[P169]
Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in submission.

[P170]
As his loyal servants cried out in rapture and madness, the unseen shadow waved a hand.

[P171]
The crimson-black flames vanished, and darkness returned.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

[P5]
*I’m back.*

[P6]
Back in the Murim.

[P7]

[P8]
*I’ve had way too much going on.*

[P9]
The Murim. The modern world.

[P10]

[P11]
“……”

[P13]
Anyway…

*Ah. I don’t want to get up.*

[P17]
“Hmm. You’re asking what kind of person Captain is?”

[P18]
“Yes. I’ve been curious for a while. The other two aren’t here yet, and I’m bored. You’re curious too, aren’t you, Escort Song?”

[P19]

[P20]
“Not particularly.”

[P24]
“……I’m a little curious.”

[P25]
Money-grubbing bastard.

[P26]

[P27]
“Hmm. This is hard to answer. Captain’s definitely still asleep, right?”

[P28]
“Yes. Yes.”

[P29]
“He is. His breathing is steady.”

[P30]
“Well, once he falls asleep, he wouldn’t notice if a ghost carried him away.”

[P31]
Steady, my ass.

[P32]

[P33]

[P34]
“Our captain is that famous, really famous… uh, how do I put it…?”

[P35]
“A handsome, impressive young prodigy?”

[P36]

[P37]

[P38]
“……Ah.”

[P39]
“……Uh.”

[P40]
“These days, people call him the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon and all that. But a year or two ago, you’d have had a hard time finding a bigger fucking bastard. He went to pleasure houses and got shit-faced every day, stole public funds, and blew them at gambling dens. He was so bad that his sobriquet back then was…”

[P41]
“Hey.”

[P43]

[P44]
“What?”

[P45]
“I didn’t say anything.”

[P46]
“Come on. You said ‘hey’ just now.”

[P47]
“No, I didn’t.”

[P48]
“It was definitely a man’s voice. Don’t joke around. Then who…?”

[P49]
His voice cut off.

[P50]
After a short, heavy silence, someone carefully lifted the straw from my face.

[P51]
Rustle.

[P52]
The straw blocking my view fell away. In the faint moonlight, my eyes met Mujin’s.

[P53]
I gave him a warm, friendly smile. It had been a while.

[P54]
“Hey.”

[P55]
“……”

[P56]
Mujin stared down at me in silence, his gaze growing somber. Then he laid the straw back over my face.

[P57]
Very carefully, as though nothing had happened.

[P58]
“Move it.”

[P59]
“The moon must be bright tonight. I’m hearing things…”

[P60]
“If you don’t move it, your life’s going to get dark. Move it.”

[P61]
“Yes, sir.”

[P62]
The straw had stopped feeling warm and cozy.

[P63]
Like a vampire waking after centuries sealed away by an exorcist, I rose from the wagon’s cargo bed.

[P64]
Whoooosh.

[P65]
A chilly wind blew the bits of straw from my clothes.

[P66]
Ju Hwaran met my eyes and hastily looked away. By the campfire—when had he even lit that?—Song Ilseom got to his feet, muttering that he needed to feed the horses some hay.

[P67]
My shadow swelled in the flickering firelight and fell across Mujin.

[P68]
“Any last words?”

[P69]
“Captain, please. Hear me out.”

[P70]
“That’s why I asked.”

[P71]
“You said *last* words. Like you want my dying words.”

[P72]
“Probably do.”

[P73]
“……Ah.”

[P74]
“You were having a great time. As your captain, I can’t tell you how happy it makes me to see my subordinate enjoying himself.”

[P75]
That was half true. I really couldn’t take it.

[P76]
I’d busted my ass in the Murim, busted my ass in the modern world, and come back without getting any sleep—only to find my own subordinate talking shit about me behind my back.

[P77]

[P78]
“Face, arms, legs, abdomen, back. Pick one.”

[P79]
“Are those my possible causes of death?”

[P80]
“I won’t kill you. I’ll just beat you like I’m trying to.”

[P81]
Mujin thought for a moment.

[P82]
“The abdomen.”

[P83]
“Why?”

[P84]
“Wounds on the back are… a martial artist’s shame.”

[P85]
I couldn’t help marveling at his resolve.

[P86]
“What a load of bullshit.”

[P87]
“I did wrong, so I’ll take my punishment. Come at me.”

[P88]
“Since you picked your abdomen, I’ll pick the rest.”

[P89]
“What?”

[P90]
“What do you mean, ‘what’? It wouldn’t be fair if only you got to choose. I should get a turn too.”

[P91]
“No, wait. How is that fair—”

[P92]
Wham!

[P93]
The blow cracked through the night.

[P94]
Above the slowly burning campfire, the shadow of a man soaring upward with blood spraying from his nose loomed large.

[P95]
*Back five minutes and I’m already using my fists.*

[P96]
We were on Mount Daebyeol, where Anhui and Hubei bordered Henan.

[P97]
Two figures approached from the distance, with Mujin’s screams providing the background music. They were the final members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion: a pair of rootless unorthodox faction nobodies.

[P98]
“……Why are they beating him?”

[P99]
“Taishan! Is here!”

[P100]
At last, every member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s Nanman expedition party was together. I gave them a short but stirring address and turned back to Mujin.

[P101]
“All right, let’s finish beating this bastard and get going.”

[P102]
Nobody objected.

[P103]
Right now, I wasn’t Jin Taekyung the S-rank Hunter. I was the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, the orthodox Murim’s greatest young prodigy, and Jin Taekyung, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master—their direct superior.

[P104]
Crack!

[P105]
“Urgh! Aaaagh!”

[P106]
I really do love the Murim. Except for that damned Dark Heaven.

[P107]
* * *

[P108]
Not a single ray of light reached that pitch-black place.

[P109]
In the darkness, where neither sound nor any sign of life could be felt, figures lay facedown and trembled.

[P110]
Then—

[P111]
“Heaven above, earth below!”

[P112]
“All demons bow in submission!”

[P113]
The cries erupted as one, thunderous. Crimson-black flames surged up from the darkness.

[P114]
Fwoosh!

[P115]
A ring of fire blazed fiercely. Yet despite being unmistakable flames, they gave off a chill that seeped into the bones. Beyond them, someone’s shadow wavered.

[P116]
—It has been a long time.

[P117]
Man or woman, young or old—even the pitch of the voice was impossible to tell.

[P118]
The strange voice resounded from every direction, pressing down on the figures prostrate on the floor.

[P119]
—My servants.

[P120]
Everyone trembled at the overwhelming power in those two words. Some shook with fear of the absolute being before them; others with joy and rapture at seeing the one they served.

[P121]
Together, they cried out.

[P122]
“These foolish, lowly servants humbly pay their respects to the great Lord of Heaven!”

[P123]
Lord of Heaven. Master of the heavens.

[P124]
No other words could describe him.

[P125]
An absolute being of unmatched dignity and greatness. The heavens above the clouds were his palace; every lowly creature on the earth below was his servant and subject.

[P126]
No. They would make it so.

[P127]
—How much time has passed?

[P128]
Every one of them understood the living god’s question. The figures prostrate before him were servants of the Lord of Heaven, loyal and devoted beyond words.

[P129]
The young man bowing low against the floor was no different.

[P130]
“Exactly one hundred and thirty-six days since the great Lord of Heaven last awoke!”

[P131]
The fierce flames wavered at his answer.

[P132]
—Yes. I remember. Western Heaven. That was the day the child left.

[P133]
“We are deeply ashamed!”

[P134]
Led by the young man, they cried out again. This time, shame and self-reproach filled their voices.

[P135]
When the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Dark Heaven forces under his command had been annihilated at the Sichuan Tang Clan, the unexpected defeat had thrown them into confusion. They had been forced to wake their master from his deep sleep.

[P136]
“Great Lord of Heaven, never again… will such a thing happen.”

[P137]
The words came through the young man’s clenched teeth. The flames stirred once more.

[P138]
—No. The mistake was mine, for trusting you despite your shortcomings.

[P139]
“……!”

[P140]
—Blood Lord. You have your own shortcomings, do you not?

[P141]
At that reprimand, more painful than any other, the young man’s eyes trembled.

[P142]
Blood Lord knew better than anyone what the master he worshiped meant.

[P143]
*Henan.*

[P144]
The day the orthodox Murim had named the Shaolin Bloodshed was one of the most painful memories of his life. He had accomplished far less than planned, and suffered the humiliation of leaving an arm behind.

[P145]
If he hadn’t at least brought back Shaolin’s sacred treasure, the Green Jade Buddha Staff… He didn’t want to think about it.

[P146]
*The Sword Saint. And Jin Taekyung.*

[P147]
Thinking of those two bastards made him want to kill. Even tearing them apart alive wouldn’t satisfy him.

[P148]
But a loyal servant must not show such thoughts before his master. Blood Lord barely suppressed his murderous intent and spoke.

[P149]
“P-Please forgive me.”

[P150]
Whoooong.

[P151]
A chilly wind swept through the darkness in place of an answer. Blood Lord and the others huddled lower.

[P152]
Then a quiet voice reached their ears.

[P153]
—What is lacking can be filled.

[P154]
The air grew heavy. The wind stopped, and every living thing held its breath.

[P155]
In the stillness, the Lord of Heaven continued.

[P156]
—I shall fill what you lack.

[P157]
It was a command, backed by a force none of them could resist.

[P158]
Fwoooooosh.

[P159]
Darkness and shadow rippled.

[P160]
An immense surge of qi flowed from somewhere unseen and settled into Blood Lord’s body. His eyes widened with rapture.

[P161]
“L-Lord of Heaven!”

[P162]
Blood Lord and the others understood once more: the master they served was a living god, an absolute being who encompassed heaven and earth.

[P163]
They understood, too, what the power he had bestowed on them meant.

[P164]
—Tell South Heaven and North Heaven.

[P165]
Rumble, rumble, rumble!

[P166]
The earth trembled. The world shook.

[P167]
Beyond the overwhelming energy that distorted everything, his voice rang out like thunder.

[P168]
—Now… we begin the Great War.

[P169]
Heaven above, earth below. All demons bow in submission.

[P170]
As his loyal servants cried out in rapture and madness, the unseen shadow waved a hand.

[P171]
The crimson-black flames vanished, and darkness returned.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

[P88]

Crack!

[P158]
Fwoooooosh.

[P161]

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style
